messages:
jamie: heads up — seeing intermittent 95p token gen latency spikes in eu-west. Correlates with KV-cache miss-rate jumps for tenant 'orange-ml'. suspect NUMA allocation drift on shelf12. attaching quick log snippet.
priya: saw that too on dashboards, miss-rate spiking ~3x at 14:02. any batch jobs around that time?
jamie: timeline: 14:00–14:08 spike window. sample log: ```2026-03-21T14:02:13Z kv_cache: miss=0.72 tenant=orange-ml numa_node=1 pid=2345 shelf=eu-west-12```
samir: could be a noisy neighbor — large batch/throughput job stomping KV pages on same socket. which tenant was scheduled there?
vlad: scheduler shows a batch job 'bert-train' landed on shelf12 at 13:59. weird — soft-isolation should've steered heavy batch off KV-sensitive shelves.
infra-bot: alert: kv-cache-regen-rate HIGH on eu-west-rack12 — investigating (oncall: jamie)
elena: for quick mitigation we can pin orange-ml to a NUMA-bound slice or move it to a dedicated slice. moving to dedicated pool adds ~+20% cost but isolates tail latency.
priya: can we repro quickly? run: `kubectl exec -it profiler -- ./run_probe.sh --tenant orange-ml --duration 5m` and collect perf counters (numa, pgfaults, cache-evicts).
samir: longer term we need NUMA-aware placement heuristics in the allocator and per-tenant KV soft-reserve. that should reduce cross-tenant eviction noise.
vlad: agreed. short-term I'm going to evict bert-train from rack12 and force rebind. who wants to own the play?
jamie: I'll take oncall. Evicting now: `sh /ops/evict.sh rack12 --job bert-train`
jamie: evict started... 14:07
priya: telemetry: miss-rate falling back to baseline within 45s after eviction, 95p latency normalized :thumbsup:
elena: please file a follow-up RFC for allocator change + cost analysis for dedicated carveouts. tag product and infra-pri.
samir: also add a metric `kvcache_miss_per_numa` with alert threshold so we catch this before tail latency impacts SLAs.
jamie: will open an incident note and attach perf dump. thanks all.
